headline: Edouard Comes Ashore as a Storm
deck: A compact cyclone crossed near Johnson Bayou with 60 mph winds, then moved inland northwest of Port Arthur. Heavy rain and flash flooding carried the danger inland as coastal warnings were withdrawn.
body: Edouard’s center crossed the Louisiana coast near Johnson Bayou at about 19:20 UTC on 1 September [E1]. Maximum sustained winds were about 60 mph at landfall [E1]. The official intensity fixes the event as a tropical-storm landfall [E1].

Later bulletins placed the center inland northwest of Port Arthur [E2]. Edouard remained a small tropical cyclone, with its strongest winds held close to the center [E2]. Its narrow footprint concentrated the coastal hit around the Louisiana–Texas line [E1][E2].

The hurricane watch was discontinued by the later advisory [E2]. The storm-surge warning was also discontinued [E2]. Those changes narrowed the coastal emergency as tropical-storm conditions and rainfall continued inland [E2].

Rain became the central inland hazard as Edouard moved away from the coast [E2]. The forecast kept flash flooding at the center of the threat [E2]. The compact circulation kept the wind hazard local [E2]. Heavy rain followed the center inland [E2].

Johnson Bayou marked the crossing point, and Port Arthur marked the storm’s immediate inland progress [E1][E2]. The sequence covered a small piece of coast and a short span of time [E1][E2]. That scale made precision matter: 60 mph, tropical storm, landfall near Johnson Bayou [E1].

The cited official notices carried no refinery shut-in figure by the 23:59 UTC cutoff [E1][E2]. They supported no defensible claim about lost refining capacity or barrels offline [E1][E2]. Any larger industrial headline would have outrun the public evidence.

By the cutoff, Edouard was inland and the hurricane watch and storm-surge warning were gone [E2]. The landfall record remained exact: near Johnson Bayou, about 19:20 UTC, with winds near 60 mph [E1]. Edouard came ashore as a tropical storm; the flood threat crossed the coast with it [E1][E2].
